symptom: `combobox x (Association: M.Asset_Customer, DataSource: database M.Customer, CaptionAttribute: CustomerName)` replacing a widget at the top of a snippet with `$Asset: M.Asset` passed check and exec; mx check 11.6.6: [CE7007] "Selected value is not valid for entity 'Asset_Customer/Customer'. Please select the value again." Wrapping it in `dataview (DataSource: $Asset)` cleared it
cause: The association mode writes `attributeAssociation` with no SourceVariable, which means "the enclosing object", and outside every data container there is none. The engine's Association mapping fell back from the (empty) outer entity to `pageBuilder.entityContext`, which the DataSource mapping had already moved to the OPTION entity, so nothing ever saw that the outer context was empty. validateInputBindingContext judged the combo box in the context its own option list creates (argContextForOwnAction), and bindingsWithoutScope skips any widget with a DataSource, so check missed it on both CREATE and ALTER
file: `mdl/executor/combobox_association_object.go` (comboBoxAssociationNeedingObject, shared by all three callers), `widget_engine.go` (Association case, `inBuild`), `validate_widgets.go` (MDL-WIDGET46), `validate_alter_unscoped.go` (unscopedInsertion)
insight: Mendix CAN express it, but the stored form differs: Studio Pro stores the binding with SourceVariable = the snippet or page parameter. MDL already writes that from `Attribute: $Asset.M.Asset_Customer`, which gives 0 errors on 11.6.6 and is what describe prints. So the bare spelling is refused and the message names the working one. mxcli does not pick a parameter for the author, because a snippet can have several of the same entity. A widget with its own data source is judged in the context it creates, and that is right for its attributes but wrong for the property that names something on the CONTAINING object. Look for every such property, i.e. every mapping that reads `outerEntityContext`. `Association: $Asset.…` is refused by MDL-WIDGET42 (it parses as an expression), so suggest the `Attribute:` spelling only
